sections.text: Matter consists of the forms that perish; Divinity is the Supreme Self; and He who inspires the spirit of sacrifice in man, O noblest of thy race, is I Myself, Who now stand in human form before thee.
Whosoever at the time of death thinks only of Me, and thinking thus leaves the body and goes forth, assuredly he will know Me.
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्।
On whatever sphere of being the mind of a man may be intent at the time of death, thither he will go.

We had been discussing Chapter 8, Akshara Brahma Yoga, Yoga of Imperishable Brahman. The last chapter ended with Bhagavans statement that one who knows me, even at the time of death, Pryanakala, with reference to the Adi Bhuta, Adi Deva and Adi Yajna in totality will come to me. That was a statement.
So Arjuna starts the chapter with question about defining these terms. Adhibhuta, Adhi Deva and Adiyajna. What are those terms? What do they indicate? But he added three more terms, Brahma, Karma and Adyat also to be defined.
So what we have seen in the first four verses are the definitions of these terms. And we come to the last question, how the one with the steadfast mind at the end should come to know you. So what we have seen so far is the definition of Purusha and Prakriti -- that which is time-bound and that which is timeless.
The self as you consider it right now is time-bound. Therefore there is a death. Death is a milestone in your existence.
So as we have discussed last time, that these verses in the entire chapter only make sense if you take the concept of reincarnation in its essence as valid principle. But thats also not really the case because it is about the existence. That which you are talking about, the existence which I consider right now is limited existence.
Will there be any existence after I die? Thats a burning question in everyones mind. Knowingly or unknowingly, consciously or unconsciously, we ask this question -- whether you believe in reincarnation or not. No culture, no religion has ever questioned existence itself.
Every religion talks about existence after death. We have difficulty accepting the idea of reincarnation because we live in a culture bound by science and technology. Unless you are one of those who do not believe in evolution and climate change, we all seek approval from science and technology.
Therefore I dont question whether my cell phone working is the magic. We know it is supported by science and technology. Reincarnation is currently not proven from our scientific perspective.
So even when this topic came up last time, Ram had to bring university research to convince some of us that this also can be researched. But what here is indicated is the existence. That we will exist is not a question in anybodys mind.
Therefore, the incentive for terrorists to become a bomber is what? What would you do with virgins after you die? You believe you wont be existing, yet you believe you will exist and will have time to enjoy. So the existence is never questioned anywhere. In any religion, in any culture, in any thought, in any philosophy, existence is considered permanent.
There was an existence before my birth and there will be existence after my birth. But what is now important is what kind of existence I would have. So our culture has put great emphasis on planning for long-term existence.
What about short-term planning? Companies who plan for the long term make progress. Like Warren Buffett does his investment in a long term basis. Some people do investment on quarter to quarter basis.
So what we do in our life is short-term planning. We plan to have a better life in this life. One life to live is the philosophy, right? There is only one life to live.
Oh, Sastra said, no, not true. You have infinite lives to live. You have innumerable lives to live.
And therefore plan wisely so that your future existence would be happier. So these verses now try to define how to plan for a long term existence versus short term existence. See, the first thing we learn is Adi Bhuta is perishable.
That which I see has been created. Therefore the term Karma is defined. Bhuta Bhava udbhavakara idhi Karma.
That which creates Bhuta Bhava -- a being or a thing -- is karma. So anything which is created will be perishable. Anything which comes into existence is perishable.
So when Im planning within the realm of objects, it is temporary. So if I want to really plan for a real long term, I want to plan beyond the realm of perishable things and beings. That is what they call it.
You will come to me, Me, the supreme Me, the imperishable. Because there are two existence which we have known through our discussion. One is imperishable, never perishes, never changes, never have any mutation.
And the one which is constantly changing. I clearly identify with the one with changes. Because I identify with this, the body, this mind, this intellect.
I clearly know that this body is perishable. I have learned through my experiences in life, this body is perishable. And also I have observed from My inferred knowledge that people die and people bury them or burn them, cremate them, so my body will go through the same fate.
So we have come to the clear understanding that this body is perishable. What we have not yet understood is the mind and intellect. A lot of this research which we hear is all about brain, not the mind.
Talking to psychiatrists, they say we dont understand mind. We dont know how these medications work. We just know that it works and therefore it is good enough to prescribe.
But what mind is is very much a mystery. So it is possible that our ancestors did not know much about the physical senses, but they knew a little more about mind than what we know today. So they have come to the conclusion that this mind and intellect has a life of its own, beyond this bodys life.
So Prayana Kale Api -- at the time of the journey, that mind and intellect, remaining intact, is going to make a move. Bhagavan Veda Vyasa here basically reaffirms the basic principles of Hinduism or Vedantic philosophy: this body is the only thing that dies at the time of death. The jiva, the one identified with this limited mind and intellect, remains intact and seeks another state of existence to exhaust the remaining vasanas.
So Bhagavan in verse 5 gives the same answer which he gave as a statement at the end of chapter 7. Antakale Chamameva Smaranam uktvakalevaram yaha prayati samad bhavam yati na asti atra sansayaha. Only thing he does is he gives a guarantee.
Last time he made a statement, this time he gives a guarantee. Im selling somebody something, but I dont have means to support all my claims about my product. I guarantee you that if it doesnt work, you can return it to me.
Ill return all the money. So guarantee is one way of making the student or the buyer feel more comfortable. He already said, one who knows me in totality will come to me.
So he said, even at the last moment, because we have considered this life to be the only life for me to make any progress. And if I think I wasted most of my life, what am I going to do now? This is more like my music teacher made a statement to me when I went to him when I was in my 40s. Subhas, do you know that Im 47? He said, So what? Youre not 67 yet. So now if I go to him, he will say, Subhas, Im 67. And theres still time.
Even at the time of your death, if you come to realize what is truth, thou shall achieve truth. Thats the guarantee. Bhagawan says Antakaale chamame vas maran muktvakale varan.
One who leaves this body at the time of death Antakaala. At the end of this body, he leaves this body. So something is leaving.
Somebody is making a journey. That means the one who is identified with the ego has not died yet. That ego is making its own journey now.
From this body to somewhere else. From this existence to some other existence. Existence is not questioned.
It is the state of existence which is questioned here. Whether will I remain in the same state of existence that I am? Will I retain my wisdom or will I retain my stupidity is the question. One who even at the last minute recognizes the truth.
He will come to know me. He will come to become one with me. There is no question about it.
So he guarantees that you have plenty of time till you die to churn over this idea of what is truth. Even the last moment, if you have eureka moment that oh thats what it is. Bhagawan says thats good enough.
Will come to recognize me and realize me. But you still have to make a supportive argument, because we are not born into guarantees. Thats why we go on social networks and say, What are the comments other people have made? You know, Meena and I always struggle about exercise.
So Meena came across something called a seat and cycle. As usual, I said dont worry about it. But once we ordered, we realized there are five more payments to be made.
It was never revealed on that Facebook page -- see, there are five more payments! I said, if you want to go ahead, go. But by the time she had already pressed that button. So then she started reading all the opinions and the comments.
Theyre all pretty bad. This is not a product for elderly. You can fall down also.
It took me three times it broke down. We said cancel that order as quickly as you can. Because they didnt guarantee anything.
They only offered a free trial for 30 days. Bhagwan gave the guarantee. But realize that you will be looking for some support, watching some comments from other users.
So he makes his supporting argument. Yam yam vapi smaran Bhavam tyajatyante kalevaram tamtam eva Ithi kaunteya sada tad bhava bhavitaha. A statement of fact: whosoever you are thinking of at the time of leaving your body, that and that person alone you shall go to.
Looking at our own context of life -- who do we meet in life? The people whom we think about most. We constantly think about a person. Then we obviously make a plan to meet.
When my mother was alive, I was thinking about her the most. Every two years I was making a plan to go and see her. Now I really have not.
Even though I have my brothers and my nephews and nieces, its not that much of a pressure on me to go to India anymore. Because I was thinking about my mother all the time. I was feeling guilty that I have left my mother at the age of 17 or 18.
Never went home, never took care of her. So constantly was thinking about her. And therefore my plans will be no other vacation.
Go to India, stay with her for a few days. So Bhagavan said that it is a given: whatever is my constant thought becomes the last thought at the time of my journey. Where will you go for vacation? Not to a place you have never thought about.
The vacation you are planning for the last six months -- you have checked all the brochures, checked out all the prices, checked out all the hotel accommodations available, researched all the places to visit. Then, at the time of your journey to take a vacation -- Thats the ticket you buy and thats the place you end up going. Bhagavan says, one who is constantly thinking about me is the only one who will be thinking about me at the time of death to come to me.
Therefore the next verse says, tasmat sarveshu kaleshu -- therefore at all times, mam anusmara, think about me. And then he says, Yudhyacha this half sloka, if misunderstood, can bring down the entire generation.

Krishnas guarantee in verse 5 is remarkable: Whosoever at the time of death thinks only of Me... assuredly he will know Me. This is not about luck at the final moment, but about the power of lifelong habits of thought. The teaching Yam yam vapi smaran bhavam reveals a profound psychological truth, we become what we consistently think about. Examine your mental habits today: Where does your mind naturally drift when it is unoccupied? What do you think about first thing in the morning and last thing at night? These habitual thought patterns are shaping your inner trajectory. Just as you naturally plan vacations to places you have been researching for months, your consciousness will move toward whatever you have been contemplating most deeply.
The verse distinguishes between Adhibhuta (the perishable realm of matter) and the imperishable Self that Krishna represents. This is an invitation to shift your planning horizon. Most of our planning is short-term, this life, this career, this relationship. But these verses invite us to consider: What if you planned for your long-term existence across many lives? This week, practice the mother meditation, think of someone you love deeply, as the teacher spoke of thinking constantly about his mother. Notice how that consistent thought naturally creates action (visiting, caring, connecting). Now apply this same principle to your spiritual aspiration. What would it mean to think about the Supreme Self with that same consistency and devotion? Begin simply: set three reminders on your phone each day to pause and remember your true imperishable nature.
